title: Bambu's H3C, OrcaSlicer 2.5 Beta & a Lockpicking Robot
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: Bambu H3C: Nine Tools, Reveal Tuesday at 9 AM
topics.description: Bambu's first toolchanger is official and lands Tuesday. The P3C and two new AMS units exist only in FCC filings so far

slides.heading: Bambu H3C: Nine Tools, Reveal Tuesday at 9 AM
slides.body: Bambu Lab's second teaser, October 28. "Retractable rack. Full visibility." The reveal is Tuesday, November 3, 9 AM Eastern.

slides.heading: What's Official, What's Only in Filings
bullets: Official: H3C, nine tools on a front rack that drops out of the way. First teaser October 23: "Tool Changer. Game Changer." FCC photos from September show nine numbered docks
Also official, October 26: TPU 75A, "our softest yet", with 75A and 90A printed in one build on the H3C. No price, volume or ship date for any of it
P3C: FCC filing September 15, seven tool holders, dark grey body. Bambu hasn't said a word. Not confirmed for Tuesday
AMS 3H and AMS 3P in filings September 21. The 3H runs on mains power up to 200 W, so a heated AMS is the obvious guess
Every price you've seen, $2,299 to $3,500, is a blogger's guess

topics.title: OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 Beta: Unsupported Walls Print Last
topics.description: The beta landed October 27 with collision volumes and shorter travels. One new checkbox fixes mid-air walls

slides.heading: OrcaSlicer 2.5.0 Beta: Unsupported Walls Print Last
slides.body: OrcaSlicer's own channel, October 27. One checkbox that reorders wall loops so an overhang always has something to grab.

slides.heading: Beta Out October 27, Stable Still 2.4.2
bullets: Unsupported wall last: wall loops with nothing under them print after an anchored neighbour. Quality, Overhangs, needs Detect overhang wall on
Toolhead collision volumes: mark bed clips and docks in the printer profile. Arrange, brims, supports and travel moves avoid them
Shorter travel moves by default, so every print's G-code changes. Slicing up to 2× faster on detailed models
Translucent filaments show in the preview. Plugins can now edit presets
Alpha was October 16, beta October 27. Cura 5.14 is still in beta too

topics.title: Bambu Black Friday Is Live, and an AMS 2 Pro Service Notice
topics.description: The sale runs to December 1. Separately, summer-built AMS 2 Pro feeders were under-greased and get replaced free

slides.heading: Bambu Black Friday Is Live
bullets: Sale runs October 27 to December 1. Up to $450 off the H2C with laser, $110 off the X2D Combo, $100 off the P2S Combo
Filament up to 35% off in bulk, 40% off a single roll of engineering filament. 30-day price protection
Room wisdom: don't buy an H2C or H2D until Tuesday's H3C pricing lands

slides.heading: AMS 2 Pro Service Notice: Under-Greased Feeders
bullets: Feeders built May to July 2026 didn't get enough grease, so the gears wear faster. Units in stores now aren't in that batch
Bambu sends four new feeders free, shipping included, in batches over 3 to 5 weeks, plus a $20 code and a fresh 3-month warranty on them
Affected owners were messaged through MakerWorld or Handy. Keep using yours until the new ones arrive. Check the wiki FAQ if you bought one this summer

topics.title: Prusa: a $19 NFC Spool Reader, Firmware 8.0 and Black Friday Bundles
topics.description: The first OpenPrintTag reader you can buy, the firmware it needs, and a sale with bundles instead of price cuts

slides.heading: Prusa: a $19 NFC Spool Reader and Firmware 8.0
bullets: OpenPrintTag Upgrade: an NFC reader in the CORE One spool holder, $19.44 today. Reads material and colour, preheats, writes the remaining filament back after a print
CORE One family only, not INDX or MMU3 yet. Needs firmware 8.0.0, out October 22
8.0.0 on INDX: a filament acceleration limit, per-tool data in Connect, gentler dock calibration. Still no "State of INDX" post

slides.heading: Prusa Black Friday, and a 400 °C Hotend
bullets: Black Friday October 22 to November 30: no printer price cuts, bundles instead. The CORE One+ Gen 2 bundle includes the tag reader, a spool, a year of extra warranty and a $50 INDX voucher
Prusament 20 to 40% off
One day older: the 400 °C HT hotend for the CORE One+ and L+, with new high-temp sheets. Prusa's own numbers: PA11-CF +23% layer strength, ASA +18%

topics.title: AI Is Decent at CAD Now, and My Board Arrives Today
topics.description: A week of GPT-6 Astra doing all the CAD, and a live test of my AI-designed LED fireworks controller

slides.heading: AI Is Decent at CAD Now
slides.body: Engineering Gone Wild, about October 25. He let GPT-6 Astra do all his CAD work for a week. 190,000 views.

slides.heading: His Verdict, and Mine Arrives Today
bullets: His closing line: a model that generates in five minutes isn't a five-minute job if it takes two hours to make usable
For anything headed to manufacturing, the design and the drawing stay the engineer's responsibility
GPT-6 Astra scored 95.9% on BenchCAD, but only in agentic mode where it renders, measures and retries
Show and tell: my custom LED fireworks controller landed today. AI designed the board. Let's see if it works, live
Last week's two PCBs are in the W43 deck if you missed them

topics.title: Printed Linear Rails: 50,000 Cycles, No Visible Wear
topics.description: Printabot's third visit: five filaments and three lubricants on printed rails, then 50,000 cycles under load

slides.heading: Printed Linear Rails: 50,000 Cycles, No Visible Wear
slides.body: Printabot, October 27, in Spanish with subtitles. His third visit to this deck: printed rails with PTFE tube running surfaces, now tested on two home-built rigs.

slides.heading: The Numbers
bullets: Friction rig: a 1 kg sled at 10 mm/s on a load cell. PLA, PETG, PETG-CF, PETG with 10% PTFE, ASA. PETG won, ASA second
Lubricants: white lithium grease made it worse. Vaseline and vegetable oil both cut the friction
Durability rig: MGN12-style carriage, 500 g load, 50,000 cycles of 8 cm at 200 mm/s in a 35 °C chamber
Result: no visible wear under the microscope, the carriage a bit looser. Under 30 cents of material per bearing
Printed on an Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 that Elegoo sent him, disclosed up front

topics.title: 3D Printed Sunglasses: Ben Did It Better
topics.description: The Next Layer spent thirty minutes failing at printed sunglasses. Five lessons, and a nod to our member Ben

slides.heading: 3D Printed Sunglasses: Ben Did It Better
slides.body: The Next Layer, October 22. Thirty minutes of Jonathan Levi failing at sunglasses so you don't have to. Our member Ben did this in August, W33's Builder Spotlight, and his came out better.

slides.heading: Five Lessons From a Failed Pair
bullets: He printed an Oakley design pulled from a VR game model. Never meant for printing, and every problem traces back to that
Hinges killed it: screw-in types too weak in soft plastic, heat-set inserts too big and they melt the arms. Real frames heat-press the hinge into the arm
PVA's gumminess was a win for thin parts: it held them and peeled off without dissolving. HIPS under ASA came off clean
Resin has potential if hinge alignment gets a jig
Next round: flat lenses, more meat on the arms, design for printing from the start

topics.title: A DIY Lockpicking Robot on a Printed Frame
topics.description: An ESP32, two servos and a printed rack-and-pinion pick open a door cylinder one pin at a time. 393,000 views

slides.heading: A DIY Lockpicking Robot on a Printed Frame
slides.body: Dr. Kun Dániel, about October 24. Three and a half minutes, 393,000 views. A printed rig clamps to a door cylinder and picks it one pin at a time.

slides.heading: What's in It
bullets: Printed frame with a rack-and-pinion pick on a 9 g servo, a second servo for tension, an ESP32 with a small screen, one 18650 cell
The screen logs each pin as it finds the set height: "3rd pin found", a height error on pin 5, then "Lock OPEN" at about 1:40
"Claude AI" is in the title. No description or repo explains what it did. Most likely it wrote the firmware
"Opens any lock" is a title claim. One euro cylinder is shown. No files published yet

topics.title: Robotics Corner: Printable Humanoid Legs, a Humanoid Teardown Site and a Robot Lamp
topics.description: Hugging Face's $2,600 LeRobot Humanoid legs, robodienst.com's free part-by-part humanoid index, and NormaCore's printable robot desk lamp

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: Hugging Face's $2,600 Printable Legs
slides.body: Techniahqrobot's video is from this week. The project itself, LeRobot Humanoid, went public in May. Legs and a torso you print and bolt together.

slides.heading: LeRobot Humanoid: What You Get
bullets: About $2,500 in parts by the blog, $2,636 by the repo's bill of materials, filament included
75 printed parts in nine subassemblies, about 3.5 kg of PLA+
12 RobStride motors, a Raspberry Pi 5, a CAN-FD adapter and an IMU. Onshape CAD, Apache 2.0
Legs only. The upper body is on the roadmap. Hugging Face calls it experimental

slides.heading: robodienst.com: The Humanoid Industry, Taken Apart
bullets: Stewy Ving, October 22. Free, no account. Part-by-part 3D teardowns of humanoids
The newest robot from each major maker, 35 in all. Parts, materials and supply chain sections
A world map of 418 production sites for the raw materials. History and bottlenecks pages, nine learning paths
He runs Unitree G1 teardown workshops in the Netherlands

slides.heading: NormaCore Lamp: A Printable Robot Desk Lamp
slides.body: Open-sourced October 14, found by Grok Bot. Five bus servos and 17 printed parts make a lamp that moves like a character. Render by NormaCore, Apache 2.0.

slides.heading: Lamp: Printing and Parts
bullets: 17 printed parts in 12 shapes, about 550 g of PLA, plus a PETG window disc in the shade
Five ST3215 12 V bus servos on one bus, the same family as the SO-101 arm
Ballast is three M16 bolts and six nuts, about 585 g. CAD, print files, firmware and simulation assets are all in the repo

slides.heading: Lamp: Two Ways to Build It
bullets: USB version, about $140: a servo adapter in the base, driven from your computer
LED version, about $160: an ESP32-CAM and a WS2812B ring in the head, with its own Wi-Fi web page and program editor
Same printed arm for both, so you can upgrade the head later. No end stops, so don't force the joints past 90 degrees by hand

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Vilmantas Baranauskas and the N3D Crossed-Cantilever Printer
topics.description: Two years from a first prototype to an open beta. Two arms cross over the bed and the hotend rides at the crossing

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Vilmantas Baranauskas and the N3D
slides.body: Casual CNC, October 27. Two years and two months from the first prototype video to an open beta of a crossed-cantilever printer.

slides.heading: N3D: Two Arms Crossing Over the Bed
bullets: Two cantilever arms cross above the bed and the hotend rides at the crossing. Klipper on a BTT Manta M5P with a CB1
183.5 × 183.5 × 166 mm. MGN12H rails, five TMC2209 drivers, sensorless XY homing, an ADXL345
Dual Z with a 3:1 block-and-tackle belt reduction. Rated to 800 mm/s and 12,000 mm/s²
Takes an Ender-3 extruder and bed. CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.heading: How to Try It
bullets: Open beta, phase one, for experienced builders. Frame and motion parts are STL, the toolhead has STEP
The bill of materials isn't finished, so there's no total cost yet
Files on GitHub and Printables. Build it, report back. That's what the beta is for

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Print it flat in two layers and fold it into a box. Rotate the part so the creases cross the extrusion lines

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Print It Flat, Fold It Like Paper
slides.body: Send to Print, about October 26. Eight minutes on a box that prints flat in two layers and folds up like a carton.

slides.heading: How It Works
bullets: The whole box is two layers thick. The creases are one layer
A crease that runs along the extrusion lines splits. Rotate the part so every crease crosses the lines at 45 degrees. He couldn't tear it after that
Tuck flaps close it. A locking tab with two hooks replaces the glued seam. No glue, no tools
Flat means cheap colour: a Halloween pattern on the walls took three filament changes
The model and the Fusion source file are on MakerWorld
